title: DoCeph: DPU-Offloaded Messaging in Ceph for Reduced Host CPU Utilization
problem: Ceph distributed object store imposes substantial CPU overhead on host systems due to its messenger layer, limiting overall system efficiency and scalability for storage workloads.
motivation: Storage I/O is increasingly CPU-bound in modern datacenters. Offloading communication to specialized DPU hardware can reduce host CPU overhead and improve overall throughput, particularly for large object transfers.
method: Ceph's communication system is moved to a specialized processor called a DPU (Data Processing Unit), keeping the actual storage work on the main CPU. For metadata operations, it uses lightweight RPC (a way to invoke functions remotely), and for data movement, it uses DMA—a hardware feature that moves data between computers without the main CPU handling it. To work around limits on how much data hardware can move at once, it pipelines operations by overlapping data transmission with buffer preparation, so the system doesn't stall waiting for either to finish.
key_novelty: Offloading Ceph's communication to a specialized processor (a DPU) and pipelining data transfers—sending while preparing space—to reduce CPU work.
contributions: DPU-offloaded Ceph architecture reducing host CPU usage by up to 92%
Lightweight RPC protocol for metadata operations on DPU
DMA-based data transfer for efficient bulk movement
Pipelining technique overlapping transmission with buffer preparation
Implementation on NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPU platform
Demonstration of larger benefits for large object writes (>1 MB)
limitations: Evaluation focuses on object writes; potential impact on metadata-heavy workloads not fully explored.
